name: Marshall 1959 Super Lead 'Plexi' (1968-69, 100 W, 4 x EL34)
description: Marshall JMP 1959 Super Lead 100 W as drawn on the July 1970 Unicord service schematic (70-6-11, the late-plexi split-cathode circuit), from input jack to a 1960 4x12 cab. Guitar into Channel I High with the classic jumper (Channel I Low patched to Channel II High), so both channels mix as on a jumpered amp. V1 (12AX7): Channel II 'normal' triode 100 kΩ plate, 820 Ω / 250 µF cathode, 0.022 µF to Volume II; Channel I 'high treble' triode 100 kΩ plate, 2.7 kΩ / 0.68 µF cathode, 0.0022 µF to Volume I with the 5000 pF bright cap from the top of the pot to the wiper. 1 MΩ audio volumes, mixed through two 470 kΩ resistors (500 pF across Channel I's) onto V2A (100 kΩ plate, 820 Ω / 0.68 µF cathode), DC-coupled into the V2B cathode follower (100 kΩ cathode resistor, plate straight to B+) that drives the Marshall treble/bass/middle stack (500 pF, 33 kΩ slope, 0.022 µF bass and middle caps, 250 kΩ treble, 1 MΩ bass, 25 kΩ middle with the middle cap on its wiper). 0.022 µF into the 12AX7 long-tail-pair phase inverter (82 kΩ / 100 kΩ plates, 47 pF between them, 470 Ω shared cathode, 1 MΩ grid leaks, 10 kΩ tail); 47 kΩ global feedback from the 16 Ω tap enters the bottom of the tail and, through 0.1 µF, the second grid; the 5 kΩ presence pot is the tail's path to ground with 0.1 µF on its wiper. 0.022 µF / 220 kΩ into 4 x EL34 at fixed bias with 5.6 kΩ grid stoppers and 1 kΩ screen resistors (solved as two matched parallel pairs), 1.7 kΩ plate-to-plate output transformer, 16 Ω tap into four 16 Ω 12-inch speakers wired series-parallel (16 Ω). Supply: silicon bridge (4 x A10D10) on the HT winding (modelled as the equivalent two-diode full-wave), 2 x 100 µF in series at the OT centre tap, choke to the screens (2 x 100 µF in series with 2 x 56 kΩ balancing), 20 kΩ to the phase inverter (2 x 50 µF), 10 kΩ to V2 (50 µF), 10 kΩ to V1 (50 µF). Standby closed, no master volume. Signal cut: the V2B cathode-follower output (about 600 Ω) feeds the tone stack through a one-sample current coupling (the stack, 33 kΩ and up, loads it by about 2 %), so the preamp (V1 + V2, 8 ports) and the tone stack + PI + power stage + NFB loop (11 ports) solve separately; against the uncut circuit the cut changes the speaker output by 0.01 % NRMSE at 10 mV input and 0.12 % driven hard (0.3 V). Input: the amp is modelled jumpered, the classic way a Super Lead is played: the guitar into Channel I High, a patch cable from Channel I Low to Channel II High (node jmp), so Volume I and Volume II both blend (Volume I at 0 still passes Channel II; both at 0 is silent). The drawing has four independent jacks; the jumper is the cable, not internal wiring (VERIFY_BATCH_2 92000 #1 reviewed 2026-11-12: kept, since unjumpered would leave the catalogue's Volume II dead).

sources.title: Marshall 1959 schematic, Unicord Inc. drawing 70-6-11 rev B, July 1970 (late-plexi Super Lead: split V1 cathodes 820 Ω/250 µF and 2.7 kΩ/0.68 µF, .0022 and .022 couplers, .005 bright cap, 470 kΩ mixers with 500 pF, V2A 820 Ω (1 kΩ)/.68 µF, 500 pF / 33 kΩ / .022 / .022 stack with 250 kΩ, 1 MΩ, 25 kΩ, PI 82k/100k/47 pF/470/10k/1M, 47 kΩ NFB from 16 Ω, 5 kΩ presence + .1 µF, .022 µF / 220 kΩ, 5.6 kΩ stoppers, 1 kΩ screens, choke, 20 kΩ / 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ droppers, 4 x A10D10 bridge, 2 x 100 µF series stacks with 56 kΩ balancing), as hosted by Dr Tube

Marshall 100 W voltage chart (Unicord, 1970, for the 1959 Mk II; same preamp): power plates 453 V, screens 450 V, V1 135/1.0 and 195/1.5 V, V2 153/1.1 and 260/153/153 V, V3 210/18.5 and 195/18.5 V, 'primary current 1.2-1.3 A at 120 VAC'
Hoffman Amplifiers forum, 'Pin voltages for 100 watt Plexi' (the Marshall chart reprinted in A. Pittman's book; centre tap to the junction of the two series reservoir caps)

Marshall '100 Watt Amplifier Type #2 c.1967' hand-drawn schematic with node voltages 270/300/375/460 V and a 20 H choke (earlier variant: 8.2 kΩ screen-to-PI dropper, 250 pF stack, 0.1 µF PI couplers), as hosted by Dr Tube

Marshall 1959 STD preamp and output stage/PSU drawings, issue 4/5 1988 (reissue: 470 pF / 220 kΩ lin treble / 1 MΩ log bass / 22 kΩ lin middle, 4 x 1N4007 bridge with 'C.T. unused', 1 kΩ 5 W screens, 5k6 stoppers, 100 kΩ NFB, 4.7 kΩ + 22 kΩ presence), as hosted by ampwares

Rob Robinette, 'How the Marshall Plexi, 2204 and JCM800 Amplifiers Work' (signal path, Channel I 2.7 kΩ/.68 µF and .0022 µF, Channel II 820 Ω/330 µF and .022 µF, 470 kΩ mixers with 470 pF, 1 kΩ 5 W screens, 220 kΩ grid leaks, 5 kΩ presence on early amps)

Metropoulos forum, 'Jimmy Page Marshall Super Lead' and '1968 vs 1969 Super Lead sound' threads (820 Ω/.68 µF on V1b in late 1967-68, 2.7 kΩ/.68 µF from early 1969; 5000 pF bright cap on 1968 Super Leads)
Metropoulos Metro-Plex MK II product page ('68 Super Lead #12380 copy: 5,000 pF bright cap)
Mercury Magnetics, Marshall replacement transformers (100 W Plexi/JMP OT, 1.7 kΩ primary, 4/8/16 Ω)
Merren Audio, Marshall 100 W replacement output transformer (Dagnall C1998 reproduction, 1.75 kΩ primary, 4/8/16 Ω)
N. Koren, 'Improved vacuum tube models for SPICE simulations': 12AX7 and EL34 laws (library models)

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS calibrated (2026-11-09) to the mean RMS match gain (-22.7 dB) of the circuit_ab settings against the legacy model, so the A/B sits at the legacy loudness on average across clean and driven settings; final level is a listening-review decision

newton.note: Event substeps (docs §10.64): the tube ports of every LTE substep converge at 10x the full step's tube tolerance; every other port and the full step keep theirs. 9900X real / driven -3.6 / -4.8 %, block p99 -8.4 %; M4 Pro instructions mean / p99 -4.5 / -9.6 %. Engine fine-step truth within 0.4 %, SPICE gate within 0.001 % (abs), aliasing within 0.2 dB of 1x on both tones. CE_SUBTOL=1 restores 1x.

controls.label: Volume I
controls.note: Channel I (high treble): 1 MΩ audio taper with the 5000 pF bright cap from the top of the pot to the wiper

controls.label: Volume II
controls.note: Channel II (normal): 1 MΩ audio taper; heard through the jumper cable

controls.label: Treble
controls.note: 250 kΩ linear, wiper = stack output to the phase inverter

controls.label: Middle
controls.note: 25 kΩ to ground with the middle cap on its wiper

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: 1 MΩ audio taper as a rheostat

controls.label: Presence
controls.note: 5 kΩ from the feedback node to ground, 0.1 µF from its wiper to ground: clockwise shunts the treble out of the feedback

controls.label: Power
controls.note: Catalogue control with no part in the 1959 circuit (there is no master volume or power scaling); stored for preset compatibility only

controls.label: Variac
controls.note: Variac: scales the mains (every transformer secondary, including the bias winding) from 75 % at 0 through nominal at 0.5 to 108 % at 1 (90 / 120 / 130 VAC on a 120 V amp)
controls.modNote: Not on the original amplifier: a variac on the mains, as players did to run the amp at lower line voltage. Offered as a mod; at full scale the amp sees its rated mains.

controls.label: Sag
controls.note: Stored for presets; sag now emerges from the silicon supply, choke and droppers

controls.label: Response
controls.note: Catalogue control with no part in the circuit; stored for preset compatibility only

controls.label: Bias
controls.note: Stored for presets; bias is a fixed -38 V supply in v1 (the 1968-69 UK amp had a fixed, non-adjustable bias network)

controls.label: G4M

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Catalogue stereo parameter; the circuit is mono, stored only

parts.label: HT secondary (equivalent half)
parts.note: unverified: HT winding voltage not on any source; amplitude set so the plates sit at the chart's 453 V at idle. The real amp is a bridge on one HT winding whose centre tap goes to the junction of the series reservoir caps; that equals a two-diode full-wave from anti-phase sources of the full-winding peak (one diode drop fewer). A floating winding cannot be expressed with ground-referenced V sources

parts.label: HT winding + reflected primary resistance
parts.note: unverified: mains transformer regulation assumed (12 Ω per leg: HT winding DCR plus reflected primary resistance of a transformer drawing 1.2-1.3 A at 120 VAC)

parts.label: HT winding + reflected primary resistance
parts.note: unverified: see RPTA

parts.label: Bridge rectifier (A10D10)
parts.note: 4 x A10D10 silicon bridge on the 1970 schematic (4 x 1N4007 on the reissue); 1N4001 model

parts.label: Reservoir (plates)
parts.note: 2 x 100 µF in series (centre tap to their junction)

parts.label: Choke DCR
parts.note: unverified: choke DCR not in any source; 150 Ω assumed for a small screen-supply choke

parts.label: Choke (screens)
parts.note: unverified: '20 H' read from the c.1967 hand-drawn schematic; the 1970 drawing shows the choke without a value

parts.label: Screen filter
parts.note: 2 x 100 µF in series

parts.label: Balancing resistors
parts.note: 2 x 56 kΩ across the series screen-filter caps

parts.label: Dropper to PI (20 kΩ 1 W)
parts.note: unverified (sources disagree): 20 kΩ 1 W on the 1970 Unicord drawing (consistent with its voltage chart: 260 V at V2 needs about 20 kΩ); the c.1967 drawing has 8.2 kΩ and the 1988 reissue 10 kΩ

parts.label: PI node filter
parts.note: unverified: the 1970 drawing shows two 50 µF sections on this node (read as parallel); the reissue has 50 µF

parts.label: Bias supply
parts.note: unverified: EL34 bias voltage. Real network (1970): diode from the HT winding via 27 kΩ, 8 µF, 15 kΩ, 8 µF, 47 kΩ + 27 kΩ divider; the chart's -51 V is for the 6550 Mk II. -38 V is a typical EL34 setting at 453 V (about 35 mA per tube in the library model)

parts.label: Channel I Low stopper (jumper end)
parts.note: unverified: jack switching simplified. With plugs in Channel I High and Low, each tip reaches V1b through its own 68 kΩ; the jumper ties Channel I Low to Channel II High

parts.label: Channel II Low stopper
parts.note: empty Low jack: its switch ties its tip to the High tip, so the two 68 kΩ are in parallel
unverified (sources disagree): 250 µF on the 1970 drawing; 330 µF per Robinette, later amps and the reissue

unverified (varies within 1968-69): 2.7 kΩ from early 1969 (1970 drawing, Robinette); late-1967/1968 amps used 820 Ω here. Separate cathodes on both: the shared 820 Ω / 250 µF cathode (the task brief's assumption) belongs to the 1965-67 amps

parts.label: Bright cap 5000 pF (.005 µF)
parts.note: 5000 pF on the 1970 drawing and per Metropoulos for 1968 Super Leads; some sources (Wikipedia, MetroAmp 50 W kit) cite 500 pF, and some 1969 amps had none

parts.label: Mixer bright cap 500 pF
parts.note: unverified (sources disagree): 500 pF on the 1970 drawing and Machine Gun Amps' notes; 470 pF on the reissue and Robinette (who also lists 100/390 pF variants)
unverified (sources disagree): drawn '820 (1K)' on the 1970 schematic; the voltage chart (153 V plate, 1.1 V cathode) fits 1 kΩ slightly better

parts.note: unverified (sources disagree): 500 pF on the 1970 schematic and Machine Gun Amps' 1959 notes; forum reports of 560 pF on some 1968 Super Leads; 470 pF (the task brief's value) is the 1980s reissue value

parts.label: Output transformer 1.7 kΩ : 16 Ω
parts.note: 1.7 kΩ plate-to-plate (Mercury Magnetics; Merren's Dagnall C1998 copy is 1.75 kΩ); 16 Ω tap used, secondary turns 2/sqrt(1700/16). unverified: DCR 30 Ω per half and 0.4 Ω secondary, leakage 5 mH per half, lm 5 H (20 H plate-to-plate), lsat 2.5 V·s are typical-class values for a 100 W OT, not measured. Secondary phased so the 47 kΩ tail feedback is negative

parts.label: 4x12 cab: two series pairs in parallel, folded into one equivalent driver
parts.note: Four identical linear driver networks as two series pairs in parallel have exactly one driver's impedance (series x2, parallel /2): folded into one instance, the internal mid nodes sm1/sm2 were never read (2026-11-10).
